approach: Root cause: the reading gate fixes criteria from the request text, and no step compares each criterion with the defaults that govern how criteria are judged (D43: a behavior criterion's evidence is commands the verifier ran, within its grant; D115; the append-only rule for docs/decisions.md and records/). Fix it at the gate with one new check, `check_judging_rules` (surveys.rs), registered as the last `step!` in `refusing_check` (checks.rs). It reads only the parsed criteria and deliverables and costs no model call. Round 4 changes four things. (a) The command rules are only those that hold for every verifier whatever its grant: an environment-variable prefix or leading `env` (policy.rs:584-591), `cargo fmt` without `--check` (athena.toml:75, reading.rs:627), and write programs or write subcommands (the verifier never writes). The hand-copied grant table and its drift test are dropped. Checking subcommands such as `cargo doc` against the live grant is the named follow-up. (b) The cargo subcommand is found with `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand`, and None is unread. (c) The decision-id rule has no cross-criterion or cross-clause state: no 'new id' marker and no object skip, because the base-form verb-position test and the between-word set already accept the append sentences. Rules (i)-(iii) are the only refusals, so no marker can excuse them. The no-id rule needs all three of: a decision-log word, 'in place' or 'existing entry/entries', and an edit verb in verb position. (d) The dependents now list every reader of `check_reading_text` (steward queue, drain, `athena check-reading`). Other decisions from round 3 stay: cited-run spans only, the imperative `records/` rule, last step position, the three-place root-cause statement, the 13th reader-rule line, D174 appended with 'Amends D43' once, and a decision-links entry.

Split each span into simple commands on `&&`, `||`, `;` and `|`. Spans elsewhere are unread.

For a cited simple command (words from the shell-style split of the span): (1) refuse a first word of the form NAME=value (NAME letters, digits, '_'; policy.rs:584-591) or the program `env`; (2) refuse `cargo fmt` with no `--check` word after it (athena.toml:75; reading.rs:627); (3) refuse a write program: rm, mv, chmod, cp, touch, mkdir, tee, curl, wget, gh; (4) refuse a git write subcommand: commit, push, add, reset, checkout, switch, restore, merge, rebase, pull, fetch, clone, tag, stash, cherry-pick, revert, rm, mv, apply, am; (5) refuse a cargo write subcommand: install, publish, add, remove, update, fix, yank. The cargo subcommand is found with `athena_agent::policy::cargo_subcommand(&args)` (policy.rs:519, skips allowed global flags, so `cargo --locked test` is `test`); None (an unknown flag or no subcommand) is unread, not refused. The git subcommand is the first non-option word. All other programs and subcommands are unread. Subcommands the grant allows or forbids by target (`cargo doc`) are not judged. The doc comment and D174 name checking against the live grant (`c.verifier_grant(jc).commands`, reading.rs:620-628, passed in through a context struct beside repo_files, about 100 call sites) as the follow-up.

decisions.choice: Decision-id rule, applied to every criterion of any kind, with no state across clauses or criteria. Words: lowercase text split on white space, trimmed of leading and trailing characters other than letters, digits and '/', trailing '.' removed, trailing "'s" removed. Clauses: split on ';', ':', newline and '. '. An id token is 'd' plus 1 to 3 digits. A clause is read only if it holds a decision-log word (`docs/decisions.md`, `decisions.md`, 'decision', 'decisions'). Verb position: the word is the first of the clause or directly follows one of to, must, should, shall, will, and, then, please, also (an -ing form: directly follows 'by'). Edit verbs, base form only: edit, rewrite, reword, revise, modify, update, correct, replace, remove, delete, overwrite, fix, change. REFUSE when (i) an edit verb in verb position is followed by an id with only these words between (at most 3): the, a, an, this, existing, old, current, entry, entries, text, wording, title, body, decision, decisions, of; (ii) append or add in verb position is followed within 4 words by to/onto/into/in directly before an id, with no 'new' between the verb and that preposition; (iii) an id is directly followed by is/are/gets/was and one of edited, rewritten, reworded, revised, modified, overwritten, replaced, removed, deleted, changed, corrected, updated; (iv) a clause without an id has a decision-log word AND ('in place' OR 'existing entry' OR 'existing entries') AND an edit verb in verb position. All four conditions of (iv) are required (finding 2). SKIP a verb when a negation (not, never, without, no, unchanged) is within 3 words before it, or one of the 3 words before it is criterion, criteria, reading, deliverable, text or rule. There is no new-id marker and no amend/cite object skip (finding 1): they are unnecessary, because 'The fix is recorded as D174' (fix follows 'the'), 'docs/decisions.md is updated with a new decision D174' (-ed form), 'This change adds decision D174' (change follows 'this'; 'adds' is not an edit verb) and 'Update docs/decisions.md to add D174' (docs/decisions.md is not in the between-set) are not matched by (i)-(iv) in the first place. So a sentence elsewhere in the reading such as 'CHANGELOG.md records the D87 fix' cannot excuse 'Edit the existing D87 entry in docs/decisions.md in place' (refused by (i)), and 'Merge refusals no longer fire D87: append a note to D87 in docs/decisions.md' is refused by (ii) (clause after ':' is 'append a note to D87 in docs/decisions.md'). Accept: 'Update docs/decisions.md with a new decision' and 'Update docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md' (no 'in place' or 'existing entries'), 'Append a new decision to docs/decisions.md that amends D87'.
decisions.reason: Rules (i)-(iv) are the only refusals and nothing can excuse them, so the two instances this job exists to prevent are always refused. Removing the marker and skip removes the contradiction the critic found and the cross-criterion dodge. Each accept sentence is shown by the verb-position and between-word tests, not by an exemption.

decisions.choice: `records/` rule in criteria: refuse only a criterion that tells the job to edit it. (a) Imperative: an edit verb (edit, rewrite, reword, revise, modify, update, correct, replace, remove, delete, overwrite, fix, change, append, add) in verb position, then at most 2 words from {the, a, an, any, existing, old, file, files}, then a token starting `records/` that has a further path segment, or is followed by end of clause, in, to, so, directly, by, with, and, files, file, entries. (b) Passive about this change: a `records/` token followed directly by is/are/be/gets and an edit participle, then within 3 words 'in place', 'by this change/job/commit/fix', 'by the producer', 'by hand' or 'manually'. The same negation and meta-subject skips apply. Not refused: 'A squash commit that changes records/ but names no job is refused by the records check', 'Fix the records/ loader in store.rs', 'land updates records/jobs/<id>/outcome.json with the landed state', 'records/ is not changed', 'counts read from records/'. Deliverables: any path under `records/` with any action, and Delete of docs/decisions.md, are refused; a Modify of docs/decisions.md is accepted. The doc comment states that in production a Modify or Delete of a path absent from repo_files is already refused by check_boundary_and_repo_files (checks.rs:268-285), and records/ is absent from main after the cutover, so the deliverable rule matters for Create and for runs with repo_files None (`check_reading_text`, replay).

risks.risk: The matcher refuses a legitimate criterion: one citing a command as part of the feature under test, one with a decision id near an edit noun, or one about the gate's or store's behavior toward records/.

Decision edits need a base-form edit verb in verb position, only entry words between it and the id, and a decision-log word in the clause. rule (iv) needs all three of its conditions. records/ edits need an imperative or an 'in place / by this change' passive. The accept tests and 18 accept corpus cases cover each shape in the critic findings.
